expectedText:
PEACE OFFICER HIRING QUALIFICATIONS AND DISQUALIFICATIONS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for City of Springfield Police Department · Police Officer

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California law governing the minimum qualifications, disqualifying criminal and disciplinary history, and certain background-investigation obligations that apply when City of Springfield Police Department is considering Jordan T. Reyes for a position of Police Officer that is declared by law to be a peace officer position. It states facts about what Government Code sections 1029, 1031, and 1031.1, and Penal Code section 830, require, permit, and restrict in this area. It is not itself a background investigation, a certification decision, or a hiring decision, and it does not tell City of Springfield Police Department or Jordan T. Reyes what to do about any particular application. This document is distinct from this corpus's existing Live Scan / DOJ Fingerprint Background Check and Background Check Disclosure & Authorization information sheets, which address background-check procedure generally, and from the Physical Ability / Agility Pre-Employment Testing information sheet, which addresses testing under FEHA, the ADA, and Title VII: this document instead addresses the statutory minimum-qualification and disqualification standards that apply specifically to peace officer positions.

WHAT COUNTS AS A PEACE OFFICER POSITION
California law confines the term "peace officer" to the specific classes of positions listed in the Penal Code, rather than allowing a public employer to designate any position as a peace officer position by its own choice. A position such as Police Officer is a peace officer position within the meaning of the statutes described in this document only if it falls within a class described in Penal Code chapter 4.5 (commencing with section 830) and otherwise meets all standards imposed by law on a peace officer.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Any person who comes within the provisions of this chapter and who otherwise meets all standards imposed by law on a peace officer is a peace officer, and notwithstanding any other provision of law, no person other than those designated in this chapter is a peace officer."
  — Cal. Penal Code § 830 (California Legislative Information text), Penal Code, definition confining peace officer status to persons within this chapter (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=830.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Penal Code section 830's general definitional statement; it does not itemize which specific offices and classes of employment Penal Code sections 830.1 through 830.65 designate as peace officer positions. Readers should consult those specific sections, or Government Code section 1031's reference to "each class of public officers or employees declared by law to be peace officers," to determine whether a specific position qualifies.

CORE MINIMUM STANDARDS: WORK AUTHORIZATION, AGE, FINGERPRINTING, AND BACKGROUND INVESTIGATION
Government Code section 1031 states minimum standards that each class of public officers or employees declared by law to be peace officers must meet. Among these, an applicant for a peace officer position such as Police Officer with City of Springfield Police Department must be legally authorized to work in the United States under federal law, be 18 years of age or older, be fingerprinted for a search of local, state, and national fingerprint files to disclose a criminal record, and be of good moral character as determined by a thorough background investigation.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Each class of public officers or employees declared by law to be peace officers shall meet all of the following minimum standards:(a) Be legally authorized to work in the United States under federal law.(b) Be 18 years of age or older.(c) Be fingerprinted for purposes of search of local, state, and national fingerprint files to disclose a criminal record.(d) Be of good moral character, as determined by a thorough background investigation."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031(a)-(d) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, minimum standards for peace officers: work authorization, age, fingerprinting, and background investigation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes subdivisions (a) through (d) of section 1031. It does not address subdivisions (e) through (h) of the same section, which state additional educational, medical/psychological, and federal-consistency standards addressed in separate clauses of this document, and it does not address whether a specific hiring authority has adopted additional or higher standards, which subdivision (g) of the same section permits.

MINIMUM STANDARD: EDUCATION
Government Code section 1031 also states an educational minimum standard: an applicant must be a high school graduate, pass an approved high-school-equivalency test or the California High School Proficiency Examination, or have attained a two-year, four-year, or advanced degree from an accredited college or university, with the statute further specifying which schools and accrediting bodies qualify and how a foreign degree may be evaluated for equivalency.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Be a high school graduate, pass the General Education Development Test or other high school equivalency test approved by the State Department of Education that indicates high school graduation level, pass the California High School Proficiency Examination, or have attained a two-year, four-year, or advanced degree from an accredited college or university."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031(e) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, minimum educational standard for peace officers (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.)
  Known gap: The quoted text in this clause spans a line break inserted by the source page's HTML formatting between the words "high" and "school equivalency test"; the intervening whitespace was normalized to a single space for this quote, consistent with the natural reading of the unbroken statutory sentence, and no substantive text was altered, added, or removed. This document does not itemize every accrediting association or credential-evaluation service the statute lists as qualifying a high school or a foreign degree.

MINIMUM STANDARD: PHYSICAL, EMOTIONAL, AND MENTAL CONDITION
Government Code section 1031 further requires that an applicant be found free from any physical, emotional, or mental condition, including bias against a listed characteristic, that might adversely affect the exercise of the powers of a peace officer. The statute states that physical condition must be evaluated by a licensed physician and surgeon, and that emotional and mental condition must be evaluated by a qualifying physician and surgeon or a licensed psychologist.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Be found to be free from any physical, emotional, or mental condition, including bias against race or ethnicity, gender, nationality, religion, disability, or sexual orientation, that might adversely affect the exercise of the powers of a peace officer."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031(f) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, minimum physical/emotional/mental condition standard for peace officers (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.)
  "(1) Physical condition shall be evaluated by a licensed physician and surgeon.(2) Emotional and mental condition shall be evaluated by either of the following:(A) A physician and surgeon who"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031(f)(1)-(2) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, who must evaluate physical, emotional, and mental condition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the general standard in subdivision (f)'s introductory sentence and the identification of who must conduct the physical evaluation and who may conduct the emotional/mental evaluation; it does not itemize the detailed licensing, residency, and years-of-experience qualifications the statute separately requires of that physician, surgeon, or psychologist, or the California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training's applicable education and training procedures for preemployment psychological screening referenced later in the same subdivision.

CONSISTENCY WITH FEDERAL WORK-AUTHORIZATION LAW
Government Code section 1031 states that it must be interpreted and applied consistent with federal law and regulations, and that it must not be construed to permit an employer to override or bypass the federal work-authorization verification requirements stated in the cross-referenced federal regulation.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "This section shall be interpreted and applied consistent with federal law and regulations. This section shall not be construed to permit an employer to override or bypass work authorization requirements stated in Section 274a.2 of Title 8 of the Code of Federal Regulations."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031(h) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, federal-law-consistency and work-authorization cross-reference (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.)
  Known gap: This document's research did not independently fetch or verify the text of section 274a.2 of title 8 of the Code of Federal Regulations, the federal work-authorization verification regulation this subdivision cross-references; this clause states only what Government Code section 1031(h) itself says about that regulation.

FELONY-CONVICTION DISQUALIFICATION
Separately from the minimum standards described above, Government Code section 1029 disqualifies certain categories of persons from holding office or being employed as a peace officer, or from any office or employment that confers the powers and duties of a peace officer, subject to statutory exceptions stated elsewhere in the same section. Among the disqualified categories, a person who has been convicted of a felony is disqualified.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "(a) Except as provided in subdivision (b), (c), (d), or (e), each of the following persons is disqualified from holding office as a peace officer or being employed as a peace officer of the state, county, city, city and county, or other political subdivision, whether with or without compensation, and is disqualified from any office or employment by the state, county, city, city and county, or other political subdivision, whether with or without compensation, which confers upon the holder or employee the powers and duties of a peace officer:(1) Any person who has been convicted of a felony."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1029(a) & (a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, disqualification of a person convicted of a felony from peace officer office or employment (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1029.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (a)'s introductory language and paragraph (1) of the disqualified-persons list. Section 1029 lists additional disqualifying categories in paragraphs (2) through (9) (out-of-state and military-tribunal felony-equivalent convictions, certain incompetency and insanity findings, narcotics-related commitments, and specified falsification or misconduct findings), and states statutory exceptions in subdivisions (b) through (e) (including deferred-entry-of-judgment pleas, certain drug-diversion outcomes, and pardoned parole or probation officers) that this document does not itemize.

DISQUALIFICATION BASED ON POST CERTIFICATION REVOCATION OR DENIAL
Government Code section 1029 also disqualifies a person whose Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training certification has been revoked, voluntarily surrendered, or denied after the person met the minimum requirement for issuance of certification. It further disqualifies a person previously employed in law enforcement whose certification as a law enforcement officer in another jurisdiction was revoked for misconduct and whose name is listed in the National Decertification Index or a similar federally designated database.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Any person who has been issued the certification described in Section 13510.1 of the Penal Code, and has had that certification revoked by the Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training, has voluntarily surrendered that certification pursuant to subdivision (f) of Section 13510.8, or having met the minimum requirement for issuance of certification, has been denied issuance of certification."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1029(a)(10) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, disqualification based on revoked, surrendered, or denied POST certification (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1029.)
  "Any person previously employed in law enforcement in any state or United States territory or by the federal government, whose name is listed in the National Decertification Index of the International Association of Directors of Law Enforcement Standards and Training or any other database designated by the federal government whose certification as a law enforcement officer in that jurisdiction was revoked for misconduct"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1029(a)(11) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, disqualification based on National Decertification Index listing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1029.)
  Known gap: This clause's second citation quotes paragraph (11) only through the word "misconduct," at a point where the source text continues with an additional, separately worded disqualifying clause (a person who, while employed as a law enforcement officer, engaged in serious misconduct that would have resulted in certification revocation had the person been employed as a peace officer in California); that continuation is not quoted in this clause but is consistent with, and does not contradict, this clause's body. This document does not describe the certification and decertification process under Penal Code sections 13510.1 and 13510.8 in detail.

FORMER EMPLOYER'S DUTY TO DISCLOSE EMPLOYMENT INFORMATION FOR A BACKGROUND INVESTIGATION
Government Code section 1031.1 places a duty on a current or former employer, separate from the applicant's own participation in the hiring process, to disclose certain employment information to a requesting law enforcement agency conducting the thorough background investigation that section 1031 requires, when the request is in writing, is accompanied by a notarized authorization from the applicant releasing the employer of liability, and other statutory conditions are met. The statute also states that, absent fraud or malice, an employer that releases such information under this section is not subject to civil liability for doing so.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "an employer shall disclose employment information relating to a current or former employee, upon request of a law enforcement agency, if all of the following conditions are met:(1) The request is made in writing.(2) The request is accompanied by a notarized authorization by the applicant releasing the employer of liability."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031.1(a) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, employer's conditional duty to disclose employment information for a peace officer background investigation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.1.)
  "In the absence of fraud or malice, an employer shall not be subject to civil liability for any relevant cause of action by virtue of releasing employment information required pursuant to this section."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 1031.1(b) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, immunity from civil liability for a good-faith disclosure (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=1031.1.)
  Known gap: This clause's first citation quotes subdivision (a) only through its first two numbered conditions; a third statutory condition, that the request and authorization be presented to the employer by a sworn officer or other authorized representative of the employing law enforcement agency, also applies and is not quoted here but is consistent with, and does not contradict, this clause's body. This document does not address subdivisions (c) through (f) of section 1031.1, which define "employment information," state a civil remedy for an employer's refusal to disclose, address redisclosure between law enforcement agencies, and permit an employer to charge reasonable copying fees.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to indicate that you have received and reviewed this information sheet.

Applicant: Jordan T. Reyes
Position: Police Officer
Agency/Employer: City of Springfield Police Department
Date: September 9, 2026
